title: Discrete and continuous data
log: 2026-11-04T09:36:55Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: The bank point 'Types of data' covers the wider categorical-versus-numerical split (nominal, ordinal, postcodes) at Year 11 depth, while the new Year 7 point teaches only discrete versus continuous data, so it is broader than the new point and not a close enough match to adapt.

draft.title: Discrete and continuous data
card: Numerical data is made of numbers. It can be discrete or continuous.
data is counted. It takes separate values, such as 0, 1, 2 or 3 goals. There is nothing between one value and the next.
data is measured. It can take any value in a range, such as 1.52 m or 1.523 m, depending on how precisely we measure.
Ask yourself: did I count it or measure it? Counting gives discrete data. Measuring with a ruler, scale, timer or similar tool gives continuous data.
draft.remember: Counted data is discrete. Measured data is continuous.

a.q: Which of these is an example of continuous data?
opts: The time Ana takes to run 100 m
The number of laps Ana runs
The number of runners in her race
The number of medals Ana has won
a.why: Time is measured, and it can take any value, such as 14.2 or 14.23 seconds. The other three are counted, so they are discrete.
a.clue: Which one would you measure with a stopwatch?

b.q: Priya records data about her garden. Which of her records is discrete data?
opts: The number of tomatoes on each plant
The height of each tomato plant
The mass of each tomato picked
The rainfall each week in millimetres
b.why: Tomatoes on a plant are counted, such as 7 or 12, so the data is discrete. Height, mass and rainfall are measured, so they are continuous. Rounding a measurement to a whole number does not make it discrete.
b.clue: Which record comes from counting items, not measuring?

a.best: The time Ana takes to run 100 m

b.best: The number of tomatoes on each plant

problems.detail: The clue 'Which one would you measure with a stopwatch?' gives the answer away. Only the time option fits a stopwatch, so a student can pick it without knowing what continuous data is.
The right option stands out. It is the only one that does not begin 'The number of', so a student could pick the odd one out without knowing the idea.
The question refers to Ana and 'her race' but the stem never introduces Ana. The options read oddly without context, such as 'Ana is a runner.'

check.summary: The facts and answers are correct. Question a's clue (stopwatch) gives the answer away, its right option is the only one not starting 'The number of', and its stem never introduces Ana.
